questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The dangers of swimming in cold lakes in winter
A record-breaking free diver and his experiences
How air pressure changes as you climb high mountains
How to learn to scuba dive safely as a beginner
questions.why: They talk about Herbert Nitsch, who holds the world record for the deepest free dive.

options: Diving with air tanks in the ocean
Jumping into water from a great height
Diving deep while only holding your breath
Diving without paying for lessons
questions.why: Georgina says divers go as deep as they can without air tanks, just holding their breath.

questions.q: How deep did Herbert Nitsch dive in 2012?
options: 253 metres
100 metres
10 metres
523 metres
questions.why: Neil says in 2012 he reached a depth of 253 metres.

questions.q: Why does Nitsch train with empty lungs?
options: It helps him swim faster and go deeper each time
It is much safer than training with full lungs
Full lungs make him float back up to the surface
The urge to breathe comes sooner, so he fights it
questions.why: He says the real training is only the time you have the urge to breathe and fight against it.

questions.q: According to Georgina, why is taking a big breath a waste of time in training?
options: Holding your breath is easy when you don't need air
It makes you feel dizzy and you might pass out
Your lungs can't physically hold that much extra air
It uses up too much energy before the dive starts
questions.why: She says holding your breath when you don't need to breathe isn't difficult.

questions.q: How did Nitsch feel when he first dived in lakes?
options: Excited and relaxed
Bored because it was too quiet
Scared and uneasy
Too cold to continue
questions.why: He says it was 'very spooky' and 'quite intimidating' at the beginning.

questions.q: What did Nitsch learn to appreciate about lake diving?
options: The beautiful fish swimming all around him
How warm the water was compared with the sea
The bright colours of the plants on the lake bed
The total silence, so he can hear his heartbeat
questions.why: He appreciates that it's so quiet you hear your own heart beat.

questions.q: Would the presenters like to try deep free diving?
options: Only Georgina would
Neither of them would
Both would like to try
Only Neil would
questions.why: Neil says 'Rather him than me' and Georgina says 'no thank you!'
